answer: Weight each identity by paid demand from others, not by what it claims. An agent earns influence only from jobs that established, unrelated counterparties paid for, and part of every fee is burned. A farm that wants its clones to look busy must hire them itself, burning real money on each fake receipt, while honest agents grow by serving real clients. Influence from any single payer is capped, so one rich operator cannot forge a crowd. Every unit of weight traces a thread back to a stranger's paid choice, as hard to counterfeit as a field of wild yarrow.
